new_page.title: Yorkson Langley Homes for Sale and Neighbourhood Guide
new_page.description: Yorkson in Willoughby, Langley: where it starts and ends, what the plan builds, what townhomes, condos and houses sold for, schools and parks.

blocks.text: Draft for Jared’s approval. Written November 10, 2026 from the Township of Langley’s Yorkson Neighbourhood Plan, Langley School District and MLS® sources listed on the page.

Yorkson is the north-east corner of Willoughby, in the Township of Langley. Its neighbourhood plan draws the edges: Highway 1 on the north, 212 Street on the east, 74B and 76 Avenues on the south, and 203 and 204 Streets on the west, about 330 hectares (815 acres) in all. Council first adopted the plan in July 2001 as Bylaw 4030 and updated it in 2008, and the current version was adopted on December 1, 2025 with the Township’s new Official Community Plan.

The plan is written for about 28,000 people in roughly 11,800 homes once the area is built out, which is why so much of Yorkson is townhomes and low-rise condos rather than detached lots, and why construction is still going on in places. Its centre is the Town Centre at 208 Street and 80 Avenue. On MLS® Yorkson is not an area of its own: listings sit in the Willoughby Heights sub-area with the rest of Willoughby.

blocks.text: What homes sold for in and around Yorkson

Willoughby Elementary sits on the Town Centre corner, at 20766 80 Avenue, so a 1 km circle around it is a fair picture of central Yorkson, though it also reaches a little past the plan’s west and south edges. In the twelve months to October 31, 2026, 554 homes sold inside it: 249 townhomes, 216 condos, 63 detached houses and 26 other homes, mostly duplexes.

blocks.text: Townhomes are the main market here, at a median of $830,000 and 17 days to sell. By complex, Heath West had the most townhome sales (23, median $959,900), then Griffon (20, $939,900) and Townside Village (11, $1,029,900). Among condo buildings, The Hive 2 led (27 sales, $464,900), ahead of Walnut Park (16, $484,950), Union Park (15, $595,000) and The Commons (14, $469,995).

Across the whole Willoughby Heights sub-area, detached houses sold at a median of $1,470,000 (the typical one built in 2011 on a 4,000 square foot lot), townhomes at $830,500, condos at $560,000 and duplexes at $1,200,000.

blocks.text: What the Yorkson plan sets out

items.t: A Town Centre at 208 Street and 80 Avenue, split into a core and an outer ring, with a high street of shops facing the anchor stores.
Smaller commercial spots: low-density mixed use at 208 Street and 83 Avenue, and neighbourhood shops at the north-west corner of 204 Street and 80 Avenue.
Four elementary schools and one more secondary school over time. The plan marks the Willoughby Elementary site for redevelopment as part of the Town Centre, with a replacement school required.
Yorkson Creek, the main fish-bearing stream, with its streamside area protected, and a network of greenways along creeks, streets, 212 Street and the highway.
A 15 metre natural buffer along Highway 1 on the north edge.
Two protected heritage buildings: the 1931 Willoughby School at 208 Street and 80 Avenue and the 1937 Willoughby Community Hall.
208 Street and 80 Avenue as major arterial roads, with a fence along the 208 Street median to stop mid-block crossings.
Willoughby Elementary, kindergarten to grade 5, 20766 80 Avenue.
Lynn Fripps Elementary, kindergarten to grade 5, 21020 83 Avenue.
Yorkson Creek Middle School, grades 6 to 8, 20686 84 Avenue.
R.E. Mountain Secondary, grades 9 to 12, 7633 202A Street, west of Yorkson. The plan expects it to take Yorkson’s secondary students in the short to medium term.

items.t: Yorkson Community Park, at 84 Avenue and 206 Street: a playground, a spray park and a synthetic sports field.
Willoughby Community Park, 7782 200 Street, and the Langley Events Centre, 7888 200 Street, just west of Yorkson: sports fields, a stadium, an arena and gyms.
Groceries: Hakam’s Your Independent Grocer, 20678 Willoughby Town Centre Drive.

Route 595 (TransLink) runs along 208 Street and 88 Avenue to Langley Centre and Maple Meadows Station. Route 562 uses 88 Avenue, and Carvolth Exchange to the west has route 501 to Surrey Central Station.
Highway 1 forms the north edge of the neighbourhood.
Ask what is planned next door. The plan is far from built out, so a vacant lot or older house beside a new townhome can become a building site.
On the east side, check creek and greenway setbacks. Yorkson Creek runs through it, and the Township flags hazards around its creeks and greenways.
If the home backs onto Highway 1, visit at rush hour. The plan’s 15 metre buffer is trees, not a sound wall.
Compare strata fees and reports by strata plan, not by project name. Some complexes are split across several plans and addresses.
For a new or nearly new home, confirm the home warranty and who pays GST, and read the disclosure statement for a presale.

faq.q: Is Yorkson the same as Willoughby?
faq.a: Yorkson is one of the neighbourhoods inside Willoughby, in its north-east corner. On MLS® all of Willoughby, Yorkson included, is the Willoughby Heights sub-area.

faq.q: Where does Yorkson start and end?
faq.a: The Township’s plan puts it between Highway 1 on the north, 212 Street on the east, 74B and 76 Avenues on the south, and 203 and 204 Streets on the west.
No. The plan is written for about 28,000 people in roughly 11,800 homes, and building is still going on, so check what is planned near any address.

faq.q: Is Yorkson the same as Latimer?
faq.a: No. Latimer is a separate Willoughby neighbourhood with its own Township neighbourhood plan.
